newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The privatisation of a majority of the companies in which the state controls a large share is slated to continue after a slowdown this year.

- The Czech National Bank should release an analysis on the developments in the banking sector to the government and budgetary committee by Friday. The report is expected to be the basis for serious debate.
- Clients who deposited their money in deposit certificates at failed Kreditni Banka will definitely be at least partially refunded, though it is still not clear to what extent.
- Czech businesses posted a 7.2 billion crown decrease in gross profits in the second quarter of 1996 as compared to the second quarter of the year before.

- Economic growth in this quarter should be faster than in the previous two quarters. This increase is partly due to two extra working days as well as to the strengthening of Western European countries.

- Agrobanka, which went into forced administration last week, currently has sufficient liquidity and minimum reserves. Deposits, which decreased by two billion crowns, are now levelling off and Friday saw even more deposits than withdrawls.
- Anheuser-Busch announced that it is ceasing all discussions with Budejovicky Budvar and the Czech government with regards to the Budweiser trademark on the European continent.

- CZ Strojirna s.r.o., owned by CZ Strakonice, is supplying Springfield, an American firm, with hunting weapons worth eight to nine millon crowns. This should increase to 45 million crowns next year and $2.5 million in the following years.
PRAVO - Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated that one lump increase of rail ticket prices would be a "gross mistake."

- Patria Finance decreased its estimate of yearly GDP growth from 5.5 to 4.5 percent based on GDP statistics from the second quarter showing a slowdown of growth to 4.0 percent from 4.6 percent in the previous quarter which were released by the Czech Statistics Office last week.
- Investment funds and companies posted losses of 3.88 billion crowns in the second quarter compared to a loss of 2.3 billion crowns in the same period a year earlier.
